Probablemente la fórmula más famosa que:
Probably the most famous formula you are going to learn. It is said: “x equals minus b, plus or minus the square root of b squared minus four a c, all over two a”.

The sign $\pm$ is read “plus or minus” and it is the key to everything: it is not one formula, it is two. One with the plus and one with the minus, and that is why two solutions come out.

The letters $a$, $b$ and $c$ are the coefficients of the equation written as $ax^2+bx+c=0$; $a$ is the one on the square, $b$ the one on the plain x and $c$ the loose number.

Watch two things as you read it: the root covers all of $b^2-4ac$, and the $2a$ underneath divides the whole of the top, not just the root.
Los babilonios ya resolvían problemas eq: The Babylonians were already solving problems equivalent to quadratic equations 4000 years ago, by geometric procedures: “completing the square” was literally completing a square. Al-Khwarizmi systematised them in the ninth century, although he accepted only positive solutions (a negative root was not a possible length). The formula as we write it today, with letters and the symbol $\pm$, is from the seventeenth century.

The letter $\Delta$ is the Greek capital delta, and here it is read “discriminant” — from “discriminate”, which here means telling some cases apart from others.

It is said: “delta equals b squared minus four a c”.

It is exactly what sits under the root in the formula above, and that is why its sign decides everything: if it is negative, the root of a negative number does not exist among the reals and there is no solution.

El discriminante responde a «¿llega o no: The discriminant answers “does it reach or not?” without solving anything. The path of a ball is a parabola: asking whether it goes in at the top corner is asking whether that parabola meets a certain height, and the sign of $b^2-4ac$ says so at a glance. The physics engines of video games work it out thousands of times a second to decide whether two objects are going to collide, precisely because it is far cheaper than solving the whole equation.
